title: Exact immersion operations and local Frobenius on Weil stalks
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $S_0$, put $S=S_0\times_{k_0}k$ and use the bounded constructible common-stage $\Qlb$ category and its Weil sheaves and Weil complexes of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Use local geometric Frobenius on stalk cohomology as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Let $h_0:W_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be a locally closed immersion of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, meaning a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion; def-weil-open-immersion], and let $h:W\hookrightarrow X$ be its base change to $k$.

1. The pullback $h^*$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with its induced Weil structure, is $t$-exact for the standard constructible $t$-structures, hence restricts to an exact functor of constructible Weil sheaves. For every Weil complex $K$ and integer $a$ there is a natural Weil isomorphism $\mathcal H^a(h^*K)\cong h^*\mathcal H^a(K)$. If $z\in W_0$ is closed, $x=h_0(z)$ is closed and $\kappa(x)\cong\kappa(z)$. For compatible geometric points, the canonical stalk isomorphism
$$
(h^*\mathcal F)_{\bar z}\cong\mathcal F_{\bar x}
$$
intertwines their local geometric Frobenius operators for every constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X_0$.
2. Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be an open immersion, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be its base change. The compact-support functor $Rj_!$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], with its induced Weil structure, is $t$-exact; its restriction to the heart, denoted $j_!$, is exact and takes constructible Weil sheaves to constructible Weil sheaves. For every Weil complex $L$ on $U_0$ and integer $a$ there is a natural Weil isomorphism $\mathcal H^a(Rj_!L)\cong j_!\mathcal H^a(L)$. For a closed point $x\in X_0$ and a compatible geometric point $\bar x$, the stalk of $j_!\mathcal G$ is canonically $\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ if $x\in U_0$, and is zero otherwise. On $U_0$ the canonical identification intertwines local geometric Frobenius, with the same residue-field size, for every constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U_0$.

proof.text: Work at a finite coefficient field whenever a construction involves finitely many objects or arrows. In the common-stage category every object and arrow is represented at some finite extension, and equality means equality after further extension [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. In particular a Weil structure, its inverse and their inverse equations can be represented over one finite field $E$: first represent the two arrows, then enlarge $E$ to make both inverse equations hold. This does not require an integral lattice stable under Frobenius. The computations below are natural in rational arrows; their common-stage versions use the specified scalar comparisons in the pullback and compact-support functors.

Apply [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact] to the base change $h:W\to X$ (in fact that lemma allows any morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes). It gives constructible $t$-exactness, exactness on the underlying hearts, and the natural isomorphisms $\mathcal H^a(h^*K)\cong h^*\mathcal H^a(K)$ at $E$ and at $\Qlb$. Write $G_T=Lg_T^*$ for geometric-Frobenius pullback. Since $h_0$ is defined over $k_0$, $g_Xh=hg_W$. The pullback-composition comparisons give $\alpha:G_Wh^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*G_X$. For $(K,\theta)$ set $\theta_h=h^*\theta\circ\alpha_K$. These are the induced Weil structures. The comparisons at $E$ are the rationalizations of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], and those at $\Qlb$ are their common-stage maps as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; pullback comparisons: Stacks 0D6D, sites-cohomology lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text: The cohomology comparison in Step 2 is Weil-equivariant. Indeed a $t$-exact triangulated functor sends the truncation triangle at $a$ to the truncation triangle at $a$; uniqueness of these triangles [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) makes the resulting truncation and cohomology isomorphisms natural in maps of functors as well as in $K$. Apply this to $h^*,G_X,G_W$ and $\alpha$. Both routes from $G_W\mathcal H^a(h^*K)$ to $h^*\mathcal H^a(K)$ are the comparison induced by the same truncation maps and $\theta_h=h^*\theta\alpha_K$, so they agree. The Frobenius pullbacks are $t$-exact by [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact], applied to the automorphisms $g_T$.

source.place: Restriction: cohomology sheaves, with BBD 1.3.3--1.3.6 truncation uniqueness

proof.text: For the assertion about closed points, factor $h_0$ as a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $X_0$. An open immersion identifies the local rings at corresponding points [def-weil-open-immersion]. For a closed immersion, the local ring at the source point is the target local ring modulo the stalk of its defining ideal, by the affine quotient description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its maximal ideal is the image of the target maximal ideal; quotienting by it gives the same residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus $\kappa(x)\cong\kappa(z)$ over $k_0$. Since $z$ is closed in the finite-type scheme $W_0$, [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a) makes this a finite extension of $k_0$; applying the converse of the same lemma on $X_0$ shows that $x$ is closed. In particular $r=[\kappa(z):k_0]=[\kappa(x):k_0]$ and both residue fields have $q^r$ elements.

source.place: Restriction: closed points and equal residue fields; elementary local-ring quotient calculation

proof.text: For compatible geometric points choose $\bar x=h\bar z$, with common source $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The inverse of the composition comparison $L\bar x^*K\cong L\bar z^*Lh^*K$, followed by the same point-fibre functor on $s$, gives the canonical comparison $c_K:\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar z^*h^*K\cong\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar x^*K$. This uses [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] and its rational and common-stage versions in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Taking degree-zero cohomology for a sheaf gives $(h^*\mathcal F)_{\bar z}\cong\mathcal F_{\bar x}$, by the stalk convention of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] and the point/cohomology comparison in [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact].

Check the local operators themselves, using the common integer $r$ of Step 4. Let $\alpha_m:G_W^mh^*\cong h^*G_X^m$ be the comparison from $g_X^mh=hg_W^m$. Then $(\theta_h)^{[m]}=h^*(\theta^{[m]})\alpha_m$: the case $m=1$ is its definition, and the step $m\mapsto m+1$ substitutes $\theta^{[m+1]}=\theta^{[m]}G_X^m(\theta)$; naturality moves the new $\theta$ past the comparison, and associativity of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] identifies the two remaining composition comparisons. At $m=r$ the returns are $g_X^r\bar x=\bar xg_s^r$ and $g_W^r\bar z=\bar zg_s^r$. Under $c_K$, their composition comparisons coincide by that same associativity. The iterated point transports $I^{[r]}$ commute with $c_K$: apply [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2) successively to the pre-fibre composition isomorphism $L\bar z^*h^*K\cong L\bar x^*K$ and its $g_s$-pullbacks. Finally naturality of $c$ identifies the maps obtained from $\theta^{[r]}$. Thus each of the three factors defining the local operator in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] commutes with $c$, giving $c_KF_z=F_xc_K$. Taking degree zero proves the asserted Frobenius-equivariant sheaf stalk formula. All identities are identities of the specified maps, not just equality of their traces.

source.place: Restriction: local Frobenius, using its three-factor point-transport definition

proof.text: Now consider $j_0$. Its geometric base change is a quasi-compact open immersion: $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is a Noetherian ring). For each affine open $V\subseteq X$, its open subscheme $V\cap U$ is Noetherian and in particular quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], applied to that open of $X$. This verifies quasi-compactness of $j$ on an affine cover of its target. Use the compactification $(j,\operatorname{id}_X)$ in the compact-support definition. At finite coefficients its functor is exact extension by zero. At the integral stage its formula is $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n j_!(K\otimes^L A_{E,n})$. Precisely [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison] identifies this functor naturally with termwise ringed-site extension by zero $j_!K$, identifies the open adjunctions, and ensures derived completeness. That termwise functor is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $\mathcal H^a(Rj_!K)\cong j_!\mathcal H^a(K)$ and preserves both vanishing half-lines. Its output is integral constructible by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible], applied with this compactification. Thus this is $t$-exactness on the actual integral constructible categories, without interchanging truncation with reduction modulo $\varpi^n$.

source.place: Lemmas 6.1.13, 6.7.7 and Remark 6.8.15; Stacks 03DJ, sites-modules lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; 010N, homology lemma-exact-functor

proof.text: Rationalize Step 7. By [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], each rational half of the standard pair is the isomorphism closure of its integral half, and the common-stage half is the isomorphism closure of the finite-field halves. Since $Rj_!$ uses the integral operation on rational objects and acts stagewise at $\Qlb$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], it preserves both halves at $E$ and at $\Qlb$. The bounded $t$-structures and their coefficient-compatible truncations are those of [prop-constructible-truncations]. Applying truncation uniqueness [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) gives the natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^a(Rj_!L)\cong j_!\mathcal H^a(L)$. The termwise identification and its open unit are compatible with scalar extension: the tensor comparison of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] identifies tensoring an extended object with extending its tensor product, and [det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits] allows its completed scalar extension to be computed through the defining derived limit. Hence these comparisons represent well-defined maps in the common-stage category; the compact-support field-independence assertion is also [lem-weil-compact-support-finite-field-independence].

Base change $j$ along $g_X$. Its pullback is again $j$ because $j_0$ is defined over $k_0$. The canonical completed open base-change comparison [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], identified with the integral pullbacks in use by [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison], gives $\beta:G_XRj_!\cong Rj_!G_U$. Define $\theta_{j!}=Rj_!(\theta)\beta_L$. Rationalize and pass to the common stage as in Step 8. This is the induced Weil structure. The normalized open unit in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], identified with the realized unit by [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], has $j^*\beta$ equal to the identity after the restriction identifications. Consequently $\eta:L\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*Rj_!L$ intertwines Weil structures: after restriction the equation for $\theta_{j!}$ is precisely the equation for $\theta$. Finally the cohomology comparisons of Step 8 intertwine these structures by uniqueness of truncations [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1), just as in Step 3. This proves the Weil cohomology assertion for $Rj_!$.

source.place: Part 2, extension-by-zero sentence: induced Weil structures and open unit

proof.text: For $x\in U_0$, regard the same point as a closed point of $U_0$. It is closed there since its singleton is closed already in $X_0$. Apply Steps 5--6 with $h_0=j_0$ and the sheaf $j_!\mathcal G$; compose that stalk comparison with the inverse of the Weil-equivariant open unit $\eta_{\mathcal G}$ of Step 9. This gives $(j_!\mathcal G)_{\bar x}\cong\mathcal G_{\bar x}$ and intertwines the local operators. The residue fields and the integer $r$ agree by Step 4. If $x\notin U_0$, the pullback of $U$ along $\bar x:s\to X$ is empty. Apply [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] to this square, and use [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] to identify its pullback with the one in the stalk definition. Its right side is extension from the empty site, hence zero (the sheaf axiom on its empty cover forces every module section to be zero). Thus $L\bar x^*Rj_!K=0$ integrally. Rationalizing and then extending from a common finite field shows $(j_!\mathcal G)_{\bar x}=0$ as required, using [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].

source.place: Part 2, stalks of extension by zero and restriction to the open

proof.text: To make explicit the assertion about exact functors of Weil sheaves, kernels and cokernels of a Weil-equivariant map are computed in the constructible heart. The exact automorphism pullback $G_T$ preserves their universal properties; thus their kernels and cokernels acquire induced invertible Weil structures, and their inclusions and projections are equivariant. For example, the kernel structure is the unique map $G_T\ker u\to\ker u$ induced by $G_T\ker u\to G_T\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\theta}\mathcal F$; applying the same construction to $\theta^{-1}$ gives its inverse. The identical argument applies to cokernels. The underlying exact functors $h^*$ (Step 2) and $j_!$ (Steps 7--8), with the natural structures of Steps 2 and 9, preserve these universal kernel and cokernel maps. Hence they preserve short exact sequences of constructible Weil sheaves. This is a direct universal-property calculation in the fixed-pair category [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], not an assertion of a triangulated structure on the category of Weil complexes.
